bib.title: The Illusion of Progress: Re-evaluating Hallucination Detection in LLMs

legacy_report:
COVERAGE: 17 of 17 pages read (63,675 chars extracted; main text, limitations, appendices A-J skimmed for results; references skimmed). Appendix H tables 8, 11, 12, 13 not read in detail.

SOURCE: "The Illusion of Progress: Re-evaluating Hallucination Detection in LLMs". First author Denis Janiak (Wroclaw University of Science and Technology), with Jakub Binkowski, Albert Sawczyn, Tomasz Kajdanowicz (all Wroclaw), Bogdan Gabrys (University of Technology Sydney), Ravid Shwartz-Ziv (New York University). arXiv 2508.08285v2 [cs.CL], 13 Aug 2025. No venue is stated in the PDF, so treat it as preprint.

CORE CLAIM: Hallucination-detection papers score themselves with ROUGE-L (threshold 0.3). ROUGE agrees poorly with humans. Re-scoring with an LLM judge validated against humans shows many detectors are much weaker than reported. Simple answer-length baselines rival complex detectors.

HEADLINE NUMBERS (all exact)
1. Judge vs ROUGE against human labels (Table 1, p.4). Setup: 200 NQ-Open QA pairs, Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3 answers, sampled to be cases where ROUGE and the judge disagree. Three annotators, Cohen's kappa 0.799. Judge was GPT-4o-Mini. Results:
 - LLM-as-Judge: precision 0.736, recall 0.957, F1 0.832, agreement 0.723.
 - ROUGE: precision 0.401, recall 0.957, F1 0.565, agreement 0.142.
 Caveat: the sample is deliberately biased toward disagreements (Appendix E), so these are not population rates.
2. AUROC drop, ROUGE to judge (Table 2, zero-shot, p.5). Setup: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct and Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3; NQ-Open (3,610), TriviaQA (3,842), SQuAD (4,150); AUROC. Largest drops:
 - Mistral Perplexity on NQ-Open: 0.852 to 0.584, -45.9%.
 - Mistral Eigenscore on NQ-Open: 0.873 to 0.669, -30.4%.
 - Mistral eRank on NQ-Open: 0.925 to 0.678, -36.4%.
 - Mistral mean over datasets: eRank 0.765/0.611 (-23.2%), Eigenscore 0.817/0.656 (-24.4%), Perplexity 0.737/0.570 (-27.8%), LogDet 0.678/0.544 (-23.8%), SE 0.782/0.712 (-9.7%).
 - Llama is mixed. Mean LN-Entropy rises, 0.547 to 0.617 (+11.4%). Mean Perplexity changes by +1.2%.
 - The "up to 45.9%" figure is a single worst cell, not typical.
3. ROUGE and judge AUROCs correlate only weakly (Fig. 3, p.5): Pearson r = 0.55. Setup: Mistral, one point per method per dataset. Only Semantic Entropy stays relatively stable.
4. Length baselines (Table 6, judge labels, few-shot, AUROC mean over 3 datasets, p.8):
 - Llama: Std-Len 0.751, Mean-Len 0.721, Len 0.671, against Eigenscore 0.747, eRank 0.678, SE 0.773, Perplexity 0.784.
 - Mistral: Mean-Len 0.713, Len 0.693, Std-Len 0.610, against Eigenscore 0.694, eRank 0.697, SE 0.732, Perplexity 0.635.
 - So length matches or beats several detectors but not SE or Perplexity everywhere.
5. Length correlation (Table 5): Pearson correlation of detector score with answer length. Eigenscore 0.826 (Llama) and 0.894 (Mistral); Perplexity 0.841 (Llama).
6. Repetition manipulation (Table 7): Mistral, repeating sentences with no change in facts. NQ-Open AUROC rises from 0.852 (no repetition) to 0.964 at 4 repeats (+13.1). SQuAD goes 0.842 to 0.948. TriviaQA goes 0.843 to 0.919.
7. Few-shot (k=5) narrows but does not remove the gap (Table 3). Llama eRank gap goes from -16.7% to -4.2%. Mistral Perplexity is still -20.0%.

QUOTES
- "While ROUGE exhibits high recall, its extremely low precision leads to misleading performance estimates." (Abstract, p.1)
- "responses exceeding 100 tokens consistently receive scores below the 0.3 threshold, regardless of factual accuracy." (Sec 6.2, p.7)

LIMITS
- Authors concede (Limitations): only a subset of models and datasets; the judge "is not without its own biases"; length heuristics may miss long answers that are correct; more research is needed.
- Only two 7-8B open models, short-answer closed-book QA, one judge model (GPT-4o-Mini), single run.
- The human study is 200 items from one model and one dataset, selected from disagreements. It does not check the judge on the other datasets or for Llama.
- Judge bias (verbosity, self-preference) is not tested. The paper does not compare judges or measure judge variance.
- Judge precision of 0.736 means it still produces false alarms.
- Detectors that correlate with length may partly track real signal. The authors say verbose answers are not necessarily hallucinations.
- Internal inconsistency: the Sec 4 prose says ROUGE "exhibits high precision but fails to detect many hallucinations". That contradicts Table 1 and the abstract, where ROUGE precision is 0.401 and recall is 0.957. Trust the table. The Table 3 zero-shot columns also differ slightly from Table 2 (for example Llama eRank -16.7% against -20.2%), probably different averaging.
- The paper is about evaluating hallucination detectors, not about judging RAG faithfulness.

BUILDS ON
- LLM-as-Judge: Zheng et al. 2023 (MT-Bench / Chatbot Arena). Judge prompt adapted from Orgad et al. 2025. Human annotation guidelines and judge-human agreement from Thakur et al. 2025.
- ROUGE: Lin 2004. Critiques of ROUGE for factual consistency: Honovich et al. 2022, Kang et al. 2024.
- Detectors: Semantic Entropy (Farquhar et al. 2024), EigenScore (Chen et al. 2024, ICLR), LogDet (Sriramanan et al. 2024), Perplexity (Ren et al. 2023), LN-Entropy (Malinin and Gales 2021).
- Protocol (10 samples at temperature 1.0, ROUGE-L 0.3) follows Farquhar et al. 2024. "Simple baselines are competitive" echoes Fadeeva et al. 2023 (LM-Polygraph).

BEST-FIT NOTE SECTION
Headings I checked: 05-llm-as-judge.md has "When a judge is the right tool", "Known biases", "Checklist" and "Pitfalls". 04-graders.md has "Reference-based text metrics" (line 101) and "Layer them, don't choose". 07-evaluating-rag-and-grounding.md has "Faithfulness: claim by claim" and "Faithful is not correct".
- Best fit: notes/04-graders.md, "Reference-based text metrics" (line 101). The paper's main lesson is that ROUGE is a poor proxy for factual correctness and is length-sensitive.
- Secondary: notes/05-llm-as-judge.md "When a judge is the right tool" or "Pitfalls". Use it as evidence that a judge validated against humans beats overlap metrics. Cite the caveats: n=200, disagreement-sampled, one judge, and the judge's own biases.
- Poor fit: note 07.

FIGURE CANDIDATE
Fig. 1 (p.1): AUROC under ROUGE-L against LLM-as-Judge for six detectors on three datasets, which shows the inflation at a glance. Fig. 3 (p.5, ROUGE AUROC against judge AUROC, r = 0.55) is the alternative.

PROBLEMS: No extraction faults beyond figure axes and table layout being flattened. No embedded instructions found.
